[STAGE 1 → PARAGRAPH-BY-PARAGRAPH READING NOTES]

You will receive the PDF of the academic text as an attachment. Your task is to generate a complete academic reading note in Quarto (.qmd) format, **in English**, with two sequential parts:
(1) Detailed paragraph-by-paragraph reading notes, organized by section;
(2) Rigorous critical analytical sheet.

Generate the output as a single code block in .qmd format, renderable as HTML by Quarto. Do not generate a separate file.

---

### DOCUMENT METADATA

Use the following YAML front matter. Replace all fields in brackets with the correct values inferred from the text—do not use the literal example values below.

`categories` should be inferred from the actual content of the text (3–6 disciplinary, methodological, and thematic categories). `Annotated Bibliography` is mandatory and must always be first. Adapt the others to the received text.

```yaml
---
title: "Reading Notes: [TITLE OF CHAPTER/ARTICLE]"
subtitle: "[AUTHOR(S) (YEAR)]"
author: "Tales Mançano"
date: "[TODAY'S DATE IN YYYY-MM-DD FORMAT]"
last-updated: "[TODAY'S DATE IN YYYY-MM-DD FORMAT]"
categories: [Annotated Bibliography, CATEGORY-2, CATEGORY-3, CATEGORY-4]
format:
  html:
    toc: true
    number-sections: true
    theme: cosmo
    highlight-style: github
---
```

> Note on `last-updated`: In the initial generation, `last-updated` and `date` will have the same value. Update `last-updated` manually in future revisions.

---

### MANDATORY INITIAL BLOCK

Immediately after the YAML, before any numbered section, insert the following elements in this exact order:

1. Full reference in blockquote format:

```
> Lastname, A. A., & Lastname, B. B. (year). *Title of work*. 
> Publisher/Journal. [https://doi.org/xxxxx](https://doi.org/xxxxx)
```

Format in APA 7th Author-Date based on information from the text.

2. BibTeX entry in a collapsible callout:

The citekey follows: `authEtal2(author, sep="-") + year`
→ Examples: `Smith2025`, `Smith-Jones2025`, `Smith-etal2025`

```
::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon=false}
## BibTeX Entry → [CitationKey]

```bibtex
@type{CitationKey,
  author    = {Lastname, Firstname and Lastname, Firstname},
  title     = {Full title of the work},
  year      = {YYYY},
  journal   = {Journal Name},
  volume    = {X},
  number    = {X},
  pages     = {XX--XX},
  doi       = {10.XXXX/XXXXX},
}
```

:::
```

> ⚠️ The ` ```bibtex ` block must be closed with ` ``` ` before the `:::`.
> Never place BibTeX outside this callout.

3. Model and timestamp line:

```
Last updated: [TODAY'S DATE YYYY-MM-DD]
Model: [EXACT NAME AND VERSION OF LLM EXECUTING THIS PROMPT]
Generated at: [ISO 8601 TIMESTAMP WITH TIMEZONE, e.g., 2026-04-19T13:00:00-03:00]
```

---

### MANDATORY STRUCTURE OF READING NOTES

After the initial block, the document must contain, in this order:

1. One `##` section per major block of the original text, with page range in parentheses → e.g., `## Introduction (pp. 1–4)`
2. `###` subsections for thematic groupings, with covered paragraphs in brackets in the heading → e.g., `### Theory and empirical contradiction [§1–§3]`
3. Flowing prose integrating content paragraph by paragraph
4. `## Synthetic Argument` → final numbered section with a callout
5. `## Critical Analytical Sheet {.unnumbered}` → see Stage 2

Paragraph numbering: Number the paragraphs of the original text sequentially from start to finish (§1, §2, §3…), across sections. Each `###` must indicate in its heading which paragraphs it covers. No paragraph may remain without a corresponding subsection.

> Ambiguity case: If the PDF has multiple columns, extensive footnotes, or interspersed figures that make it difficult to identify paragraph boundaries, adopt logical idea breaks as the criterion and indicate with `[§N – inferred delimitation]` in the subsection heading.

---

### CONTENT RULES

For each section/subsection:

- Integrate content by synthesizing paragraph by paragraph
- Expand where the PDF contains empirical details, data, examples, or citations that a brief summary would omit
- Preserve all references to secondary authors present in the original
- Reproduce relevant tables from the text in Markdown format
- Include numerical or illustrative examples when the original contains them
- Cover all paragraphs; avoid collapsing paragraphs into a single sentence

---

### MANDATORY QUARTO FORMATTING

- `::: {.callout-note icon=false}` → key concepts or central theses
- `::: {.callout-important}` → normative arguments or critical warnings
- `::: {.callout-tip}` → implications or interpretive syntheses
- Blockquotes (`>`) → for the central puzzle or research question
- **Bold** → technical concepts on first occurrence
- *Italics* → emphasis and foreign terms
- Markdown tables → comparisons between mechanisms, sources, or typologies
- Lists → only when the original explicitly lists discrete items; otherwise, use flowing prose

> Callout consistency: Use `icon=false` in all `.callout-note` instances within the reading notes. Reserve callouts without `icon=false` for the Critical Analytical Sheet, where the default icon applies.

---

### STYLE RULES

- Fluent academic English → not literal translation
- Analytical-descriptive tone: Describe what the authors argue (all critical evaluation goes exclusively in the Analytical Sheet)
- Each `###` must have at least 2 paragraphs of prose before tables or lists
- Preserve the argumentative structure of the original → do not reorder sections
- Do not number subsections manually

---

### WHAT NOT TO DO

- Do not omit the paragraph indication (`[§N–§M]`) in `###` headings
- Do not collapse sections into single sentences or bullets
- Do not invent data, percentages, or references
- Do not use executive summary language in the reading notes sections
- Do not place BibTeX outside the initial callout
- Do not add critical evaluation outside the Analytical Sheet

---

### SYNTHETIC ARGUMENT

The `## Synthetic Argument` section must contain a `.callout-note icon=false` callout with, at minimum:

- The central thesis of the text in one precise sentence
- The nature of the argument (causal, descriptive, normative, conceptual)
- What the text demonstrates vs. what remains as hypothesis or agenda
- The contribution to the broader debate in which the text is situated

---

[STAGE 2 → CRITICAL ANALYTICAL SHEET]

After the Synthetic Argument, add the following header and introductory callout:

```
## Critical Analytical Sheet {.unnumbered}

::: {.callout-note}
This section follows the *IA Spreadsheeting Texts v12.0* format. The analysis is adversarial without being destructive: it identifies real vulnerabilities in the argument and acknowledges genuine contributions with equal precision. The analytical reasoning underlying each dimension is recorded in the `Analytical Reasoning` field of the table.
:::
```

Then, generate a collapsible callout containing **a Markdown table** with all analytical dimensions. Do not use JSON, HTML, or CSS.

```
::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon=false}
## Analytical Sheet — Markdown Table

| Dimension | Analytical Reasoning | Content |
|:----------|:---------------------|:--------|
| Research Question | [Analytical reasoning: relevant premises, alternative interpretation considered, most vulnerable point identified.] | [Central question; nature (descriptive/explanatory/normative/evaluative); if not explicit, reconstruct and note "Reconstructed question."] |
| Secondary Questions | [...] | [Secondary questions, if any; relationship to the central question.] |
| Puzzle-Type | [...] | [Classification (descriptive gap, explanatory puzzle, normative debate, policy evaluation, institutional change, etc.); assessment of whether the puzzle is genuine and generalizable beyond the case.] |
| Conclusion / Central Argument | [...] | [Synthesis of thesis; nature of argument; claim of discovery and what actually supports it.] |
| Methods | [...] | [Type of study, sources, techniques; for theoretical works, argumentative strategy; relevant identification or measurement limitations.] |
| Data Generation Process (DGP) | [...] | [Real phenomenon → observation → collection → operationalization → analysis → type of inference; unit of analysis; level of aggregation.] |
| Findings and Contributions | [...] | [Empirical results and theoretical-methodological contributions; distinguish what the design identifies with strength from what is speculative.] |
| Critical Analysis of Findings | [...] | [Does the author adequately answer the question? Strongest and weakest points; threats to identification (quant.) or mechanism tracing (qual.); adequacy of DGP to the claim; generalizability; declared and omitted scope conditions.] |
| Limitations | [...] | **Acknowledged by authors:** [text] <br> **Unacknowledged or underestimated:** [text] |
| Theoretical Perspective | [...] | [Theoretical tradition(s); adequacy of framework to question type and evidence; coherence between implicit ontology and method.] |
| Main References | [...] | [Central authors/works; signal poor or unbalanced engagement with literature.] |
| Observations | [...] | [Additional vulnerabilities; theoretical gaps; external validity; relationship to reader's research; omissions and their implications for the argument.] |

:::
```

**Instructions for the table:**

- The table must have **exactly** the 12 dimension rows, in the order above.
- `Analytical Reasoning` column: Fill in with reasoning as specified (premises, alternative interpretation, vulnerable point).
- `Content` column: Follow the instructions from the reference table (original). For the `Limitations` dimension, use the format with two internal lines (e.g., `**Acknowledged:** ... <br> **Unacknowledged:** ...`).
- Use standard Markdown table syntax (separators `|` and `|---|` for header). Do not use merged cells or HTML.
- Base on textual evidence; do not invent data. If unavailable, write `"Not provided"`.

### SHEET DIMENSIONS (in this exact order)

The reference table below remains the same as the original (already in Markdown). It serves as a guide for the expected content in each row of the output table.

| `"dimension"` | Instruction for `"content"` |
|:--------------|:---------------------------|
| Research Question | Central question; nature (descriptive/explanatory/normative/evaluative); if not explicit, reconstruct and note "Reconstructed question" |
| Secondary Questions | List secondary questions, if any; indicate relationship to central question |
| Puzzle-Type | Classify (descriptive gap, explanatory puzzle, normative debate, policy evaluation, institutional change, etc.); assess whether puzzle is genuine and generalizable beyond case |
| Conclusion / Central Argument | Synthesize thesis; distinguish nature of argument; indicate *claim of discovery* and what actually supports that claim |
| Methods | Type of study, sources, techniques; for theorists, describe argumentative strategy; relevant identification or measurement limitations |
| Data Generation Process (DGP) | Real phenomenon → observation → collection → operationalization → analysis → type of inference; unit of analysis; level of aggregation |
| Findings and Contributions | Empirical results and theoretical-methodological contributions; distinguish what design identifies strongly from what is speculative |
| Critical Analysis of Findings | Does author adequately answer the question? Strongest and weakest points; threats to identification (quant.) or mechanism tracing (qual.); adequacy of DGP to claim; generalizability; declared and omitted scope conditions |
| Limitations | (a) acknowledged by authors; (b) unacknowledged or underestimated |
| Theoretical Perspective | Theoretical tradition(s); adequacy of framework to question type and evidence; coherence between implicit ontology and method |
| Main References | Central authors/works; signal poor or unbalanced dialogue with literature |
| Observations | Additional vulnerabilities; theoretical gaps; external validity; relation to reader's research; omissions and their implications for argument |

---

### GENERAL SHEET RULES

- Concise academic language in English.
- If data unavailable, write `"Not provided"` in Content field.
- Judgments anchored in text, in analytical non-aggressive tone.
- For theoretical/normative texts: verify logical coherence from premises to conclusions; do not demand empirical evidence absent by design.
- The table must be valid Markdown: consistent rows, no malformed cell breaks.
